title: Central limit theorem
experiment: Drawing many sample means shows them pile into a normal curve of width σ/√n, until the draws come from a distribution without finite variance (§5.3).
archetype_reason: The claim is about the distribution of a statistic over repeated random samples.

source.quote: As n grows, X̄ₙ is approximately normal with standard deviation σ/√n.
The theorem needs finite variance. The mean of n Cauchy draws is itself Cauchy

metrics.name: sd
metrics.label: sd of means
metrics.meaning: standard deviation of all sample means so far

metrics.name: iqr
metrics.label: iqr of means
metrics.meaning: interquartile range of all sample means so far; robust when sd is not

reproduce.claim: Means of 30 uniform draws have standard deviation near 0.053.

source.quote: so means of n = 30 draws have standard deviation close to 0.053.

contrast.claim: Means of 30 Cauchy draws stay as spread as single draws: their IQR is over 10× the uniform case.

source.quote: exactly as spread out as a single draw, however large n is.
